verdict.rationale: Convex documents that a deployment can run locally for development. Its open-source backend, which runs the same code as the cloud service, can also run on your own machine via Docker or a prebuilt binary. However, the local-dev mode rests on a single brief docs sentence, and the main `npx convex dev` workflow pushes to a dev deployment rather than a documented local emulator. missing for 10: detailed docs on the local deployment workflow, confirmation that the whole stack (auth, file storage, crons, vector search) works locally, and independent or hands-on corroboration of local-before-deploy use.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the whole backend stack locally with an emulator or CLI before deploying

citations.quote: It's also possible to run a Convex deployment locally for development.
Self-hosted Convex runs the open-source backend, and contains the same fully up-to-date code the cloud service uses.
You can either use Docker (recommended) or a prebuilt binary to self host Convex.
Watches the local filesystem. When you change a function or the schema, the new versions are pushed to your dev deployment
